title: Smoked BBQ Chicken Wings Tray
seoTitle: Smoked BBQ Chicken Wings Tray | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Wings that smoke first, crisp second, and hold in a tray between calls
subtitle: Dry-rub smoke, crisp finish, and sticky sauce for ten
description: Adapted from classic smoked wing tradition (Hey Grill Hey, Weber): split wings get a dry rub, smoke at 250°F, then finish hot and toss in house BBQ sauce for a tray that feeds ten fast.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Smoked BBQ Chicken Wings Tray in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Season the wings
steps.instruction: Pat wings dry. Toss with salt, brown sugar, paprika, garlic powder, pepper, and baking powder until evenly coated. Rest 10 minutes.

steps.title: Smoke at 250°F
steps.instruction: Arrange wings on wire racks skin-side up. Smoke at 250°F until internal temp reaches 160°F, about 45–50 minutes. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Crisp finish
steps.instruction: Increase heat to 425°F (grill or oven) 12–15 minutes until skin crisps and wings hit 165°F internal. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Build wing sauce
steps.instruction: Simmer BBQ sauce, hot sauce, and butter until smooth. Keep warm for tossing. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Toss and tray
steps.instruction: Toss hot wings in sauce to coat. Spread on sheet pans for service. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Hold at 170°F
steps.instruction: Cover loosely with foil and hold at 170°F up to 30 minutes. Re-toss if sauce pools. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Cooking step
steps.instruction: Wings on a tray with celery and ranch. Napkins mandatory. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Leftovers
steps.instruction: Re-crisp on a sheet pan at 400°F 8 minutes. Toss with fresh sauce. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Baking powder dries skin for crisp without deep frying.
165°F is the floor—pull when clear juices run from the thickest drum.
Toss in batches so every wing gets sauce, not just the bottom layer.
tonightSpread: Sauced wings on a tray with celery sticks.
Ranch or blue cheese on the side.
leftovers: Pull meat for wing tacos with slaw.
Chop into a smoky chicken dip for game night.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Wings are handheld morale. Smoke adds depth without fryer mess, and they hold covered at 170°F for 30 minutes.
mealPrepNotes: Season wings early. Smoke in two batches on wire racks. Finish and sauce right before service, or hold sauced wings covered at 170°F up to 30 minutes.
